subject: underestimation of abundance in a dsm

messages.author: 8753e7ce2213ca31
messages.subject: underestimation of abundance in a dsm
parts:
Hi all
We are working to estimate the spatial abundance of sheep in a ranch using DSM approach. We have a scale of segment and grid of 500m side, and a total of 74 segments. We achieve models with good residuals that explain up to 60% of the deviance, using variables such as EVI (vegetation index), distance to the watering hole, using the paddock (= ranch divisions) as a factor. Our problem arises when we make predictions, which result in very low values (about 500 animals), compared with the sheep stock that we know the ranch has (about 2500). The total CVs (df +GAM) are high (between 0.30 and 0.50) but even so the value of the upper limit of the confidence interval of the estimate does not include nor is it close to 2500 animals. The spatial distribution of the abundances predicted with these models represents very well the expected distribution of the sheep in the field, i.e. the relative abundance seems to be fine.
We believe that we do not have overfitting in the variables since the edf are low.  We have a good range of representativeness of the predictor variables between segdata and our prediction grid. We calculate abundance with the classic distance sampling approach (based on design) and that gives us about 3000 animals, quite close to the real value, which we believe suggests that the problem is not our sampling design.

What do you think is happening?
Any advice will be very helpfull!

Thanks in advance
Natalia

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] underestimation of abundance in a dsm
parts:
Hi Natalia, hi listfolk,

That sounds a bit odd. One simple thing to check is that the units and
sizes are correct. For example, ensuring that the area of the prediction
grid is the correct area (and matches the area used when you make a
design-based estimate).

If that doesn't fix things, if you could send me your data and script
off-list I will take a look and see if anything else comes to mind (hard
to diagnose without looking at the model, sorry).

Hope this helps!

cheers,
--dave
